newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sees long-term GNP at 7.5-8.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sees long-term GNP at 7.5-8.5 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' gross national product is projected to grow an annual 7.5-8.5 percent from 1998 to 2000, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said in his report to the Cabinet on Tuesday.
Gross domestic product, which is GNP excluding income from abroad, is forecast to grow by 8.3 percent yearly from 1998 to the year 2000.
For 1997, the government is aiming for GNP growth of seven percent to eight percent.

The government expected to end its status as a borrowing country in the International Monetary Fund beginning in 1998, de Ocampo said. The three-year IMF extended fund facility is due to be completed in mid-1997.
De Ocampo, who reported to the Cabinet on last month's IMF-World Bank meetings, said the country's economy would be fortified if the government succeeds in completing economic reforms.

He listed the comprehensive tax reform programme, the streamlining of the public sector, the deregulation of the oil industry, restructuring of the electricity sector, further investment liberalisation and the development of the capital markets.
